title: Rapid preparation of rodent testicular cell suspensions and spermatogenic stages purification by flow cytometry using a novel blue-laser-excitable vital dye
author: Rodríguez-Casuriaga, Santiñaque, et al.
materials: The optimization of the method with a blue-laser-excitable DNA-specific vital dye (Vybrant DyeCycle Green [VDG], Invitrogen) has had a direct effect on the integrity of the purified fractions, turning them more suitable for downstream expression profiling. Besides, the inclusion of VDG afforded very interesting cytometric profiles with a significant number of cell populations distinguishable in the dot plots, even in species with no peculiar abundancy of certain stages such as L/Z in mouse [11]. Within 2C cells, different subpopulations can also be distinguished, but their identities are yet to be determined.

Any flow sorter equipped with a standard 488 nm blue laser can be used for the analysis and separation of cells stained with VDG (Invitrogen). We have used a FACSVantage (BD Biosciences) flow sorter equipped with a Coherent argon ion laser tuned to emit at 488 nm. VDG is a DNA-specific vital dye with non-cytotoxic reported effects that allows cytometric analysis based on DNA content using a blue laser as excitation source. Interestingly, it also renders differential chromatin staining patterns that resemble those obtained with Hoechst dyes under a fluorescence microscope (see Fig. 1).(1)For VDG staining, add fluorochrome at a final concentration of 10 μM to the cell suspension, and incubate for 1 h at 37 °C in the dark.(2)Laser power is set to 100 mW and a 530/30 band pass filter is used to collect VDG-emitted fluorescence in FL1.(3)Perform FCM measurements with a 70 μm nozzle. Use CellQuest software (BD Biosciences) to analyze the following parameters: forward scatter (FSC-H); side scatter (SSC-H); total emitted fluorescence or pulse-area (FL1-A); and duration of fluorescence emission or pulse-width (FL1-W).(4)For purification of testis cell populations representing different spermatogenic stages, set sorting mode in Normal-R or Normal-C, using 3 sorted drops as envelope. Keep sample and collection tubes at 3–4 °C by using a refrigeration unit. Adjust sample differential pressure to analyze cells at a rate of 500–1000 per second.(5)Collect sorted cells into 12 mm × 75 mm polystyrene tubes containing 0.5 mL separation medium. If downstream RNA extraction is planned, work under RNAase-free conditions and collect cells into sterile tubes containing PBS treated with 0.1% DMPC (PBS-DMPC). Subsequently, spin down the cells (500 g, 10 min, 4 °C), wash with PBS-DMPC, freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at −80 °C. Alternatively, cells can be directly classified onto plastic Petri dishes using Clone-Cyt software (BD), and analyzed under laser confocal and differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy to determine cellular integrity and homogeneity of sorted fractions. Moreover, identity of classified cells can be determined by immunocytochemical assays using cell type-specific antibodies. In this work, immunodetection of a meiotic cell-specific protein was performed essentially as described before [11].

steps.title: Euthanize and dissect testes
steps.instruction: Euthanize the animal according to institutional guidelines (overdose of pentobarbital; for the youngest specimens use cervical dislocation). Dissect the testes and place them on ice in a 60 mm glass Petri dish containing 5 mL ice‑cold DMEM supplemented with 10 % fetal calf serum (or ice‑cold freshly prepared DPBS as an alternative).

steps.title: Remove tunica and mince tissue
steps.instruction: Remove the tunica albuginea and cut the decapsulated testes into pieces of 2–3 mm on each side.

steps.title: Disaggregate tissue with Medimachine
steps.instruction: Place 1 mL cold supplemented DMEM and 4–5 tissue pieces into a disposable Medimachine grinder unit (perforated stainless‑steel screen, metal rotor). Run the Medimachine for 30 s, then recover the resulting cell suspension with a 3–5 mL syringe without needle.

steps.title: Filter and prevent clumping
steps.instruction: Filter the suspension through a 50 µm nylon mesh previously soaked with 0.5 mL supplemented DMEM. Add 2‑naphthol‑6,8‑disulfonic acid dipotassium salt (NDA) to a final concentration of 0.2 % to prevent cell clumping, repeat the filtration, and keep the filtrate on ice.

steps.title: Count cells and adjust concentration
steps.instruction: Take an aliquot, count cells in a Neubauer chamber and adjust the suspension to 3–5 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ using supplemented DMEM or DPBS (typical yield 4–5 × 10⁷ cells g⁻¹ testis). Check viability by Trypan blue exclusion: mix 100 µL cell suspension, 200 µL DPBS and 300 µL 0.4 % Trypan blue, then count.

steps.title: Stain cells with Vybrant DyeCycle Green
steps.instruction: Add Vybrant DyeCycle Green (Invitrogen) to the cell suspension to a final concentration of 10 µM. Incubate for 1 h at 37 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Configure flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Set laser power to 100 mW (488 nm blue laser) and use a 530/30 nm band‑pass filter for FL1 detection. Use a 70 µm nozzle and acquire data with CellQuest software, recording FSC‑H, SSC‑H, FL1‑A and FL1‑W.

steps.title: Sort cells and collect fractions
steps.instruction: Set sorting mode to Normal‑R or Normal‑C with three sorted drops as envelope. Keep the sample and collection tubes at 3–4 °C using a refrigeration unit and adjust differential pressure to obtain a sorting rate of 500–1000 events s⁻¹. Collect sorted cells into 12 mm × 75 mm polystyrene tubes containing 0.5 mL separation medium (or, for RNA work, into sterile tubes with PBS‑DMPC (0.1 % DMPC)).

steps.title: Post‑sort processing for RNA
steps.instruction: Spin the collected cells at 500 g for 10 min at 4 °C, wash with PBS‑DMPC, freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at −80 °C. Alternatively, deposit cells onto plastic Petri dishes using Clone‑Cyt software for microscopy or perform immunocytochemistry with cell‑type‑specific antibodies.
